subject: Airgapped pilot: footprint & onboarding (Private vs Dedicated)
messages:
From: Diane Park <diane.park@caretica.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask — airgapped / isolated deployment sizing and timeline

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Caretica's security team reviewed the high level architecture and we need a sizing + onboarding proposal that compares two paths: a fully airgapped Private (on-prem installer or VPC/airgap package) vs Redwood Dedicated with isolated tenancy and contractual SLAs.

Quick baseline for the pilot:
- Expected peak: 450 qps (inference requests, average payload ~1.6k tokens)
- P95 latency target: <300ms for single-shot requests
- Longest sequences for evaluation: up to 4k tokens (rare)
- Retention/event logging: strict retention rules; audit log delivery to our SIEM
- Timeline: pilot readiness target ~8 weeks from now

Can you include: estimated GPU footprint, staging vs production delta, security controls we need to provide for an airgapped acceptance test, and an estimated cost delta between the two options? If you can send a preliminary workbook that we can review with our infra folks, that would be great.

Appreciate it — Diane
Diane Park
Head of Infrastructure
Caretica Health

On Fri, Jul 20, 2028 at 10:05 AM karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com wrote:
> Team — forwarding Caretica's ask.

Quick technical notes / assumptions I added to the workbook (see gpu_cost_model.csv):
- Baseline perf: for 450 qps with ~1.6k token avg, continuous batching (target 30–40ms extra) reduces GPU count substantially. For low-latency single-shot (<300ms) we need replication headroom.
- Private (airgapped) path: recommend H100 80GB (4 x prod nodes) for initial pilot + 1 staging node; NVMe: 12TB across nodes for KV cache and model shard swap. Dockerized on-prem bundle or OVA for airgapped install.
- Dedicated (isolated tenancy): 6 x A100-80GB equiv (shared infra but reserved pools with tenancy isolation) — advantage: faster onboarding, remote patching, Redwood managed KMS integration.
- Sequence handling: reserve a quantized variant for 4k peaks; KC cache hit rate assumptions in sheet (expected 65–75% prefix reuse).
- Ops notes: airgapped acceptance test requires signed binaries, offline attestation, and scheduled on-site runbook exercise (we should schedule a 2-day handover with Caretica infra).

I've attached a CSV with the cost model rows. Numbers are preliminary; final will tie to actual SKU pricing and whether they prefer reserved monthly commit vs burst.

Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — this aligns with the commercial plays we should offer. A few commercial bullets to include in the recommendation to Caretica: 
- Option A (Private on-prem airgapped): Professional services + packaging fee (one-time), optional annual maintenance + on-site QBRs. We price the PS as a fixed milestone schedule to cover signed-binary delivery and attestation support.
- Option B (Redwood Dedicated isolated tenancy): Monthly reserved commit for a 12-month pilot with a smaller setup fee; include an SLA ladder and a 30% credit tier if we miss P95 latency targets during pilot.

I also recommend a third short note in the proposal showing a hybrid cutover path: start Dedicated for week 1–4 (faster time-to-value) and then shift to Private once the airgap packaging completes. That reduces time-to-insight and lowers risk.

I attached the internal deal playbook pages that map these options to our discount bands. If Caretica values time-to-insight and has strict on-prem constraints, the hybrid path is typically what closes.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Deal Engineering | Redwood Inference

Subject: Airgapped pilot — two-option recommendation and next steps

Hi Diane / Sanjay,

Appreciate the detailed ask — thank you. We pulled together a concise two-option recommendation and an accelerated hybrid path that reduces your time-to-insight. High-level summary below; attached is a draft proposal workbook for your infra team to review (proposal-draft.pdf).

Option 1 — Private (airgapped, on-prem package)
- Suggested pilot footprint: 4 x H100-80GB prod nodes + 1 staging node; ~12TB aggregated NVMe for KV cache and model shards.
- Expected latency: P95 <300ms with tuned batching and reserved worker headroom; requires on-site acceptance and signed-binary install.
- Onboarding timeline: 6–10 weeks (packaging, security attestation, and site acceptance).
- Pros: full control, meets strict airgap/regulatory posture.
- Cons: longer lead time, PS-heavy, higher upfront engineering cost.

Option 2 — Dedicated (reserved isolated tenancy)
- Suggested pilot footprint: 6 x A100-80GB equiv in a reserved, isolated tenant.
- Expected latency: P95 generally <300ms; faster onboarding (2–3 weeks) and Redwood-managed telemetry (audit logs delivered to your SIEM).
- Pros: faster start, lower upfront PS; Redwood handles patching and KMS integrations.
- Cons: external hosting — requires contractual controls and attestations for data custody.

Recommended hybrid path:
- Start on Dedicated for immediate testing (week 1–4) and run airgapped packaging in parallel. Once packaging is validated, perform a controlled cutover to Private if you proceed. This minimizes time-to-insight while preserving your long-term posture.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Caretica prefers us to price Option 1 as an all-in PS+license bid or to split PS + infra SKU estimates.
2) If you approve, we will: finalize SKU pricing, lock a 2-week Redwood runbook window for acceptance testing, and share a redlineable MPA.

I've CC'd Marissa and Priyom for any clarifications on commercial and technical rows.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call tomorrow to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
